item.title: @tbo.harlem: Halloween in Harlem in unrivaled, and yesterday was no exception. The community came out f

item.description:
Halloween in Harlem in unrivaled, and yesterday was no exception. The community came out for the kids all over.
From East Harlem to Washington Heights, Halloween events brought the community out to out in for both the kids and adults.
I couldn’t get to them all, but I made it over to @lamarquetanyc where they had it going ON! A circus, stilt-walkers, face painters and all.
@120thmmm was not to be outdone tho and you know they set the standards. Once again, they hosted the Harlem community and beyond as city goers from all over make the trek to Harlem for their event. It did not disappoint. 🔥🔥🔥
Lastly I made it over to the @plazaeventsharlem at the ACP State Office Building just in time to catch @jmosesharper and the students from @hsanyc perform “Thriller”. 🔥❤️🔥
The streets were alive and small businesses all over gave out candy and treats making This Harlemween’s one of my favorites ever! Bravo Harlem! 👏🏽👏🏽❤️❤️🔥🔥 Thanjs for a job well done. - #harlem #tboharlem #harlemween #halloween #nyc

item.title: @gagosian: “Friends and Legends: The Collection of Michael Chow,” a two-part presentation of major wo
item.author: @gagosian
item.description:
“Friends and Legends: The Collection of Michael Chow,” a two-part presentation of major works from the collection of Michael Chow (@mrchow), debuts at the gallery’s Beverly Hills location this Thursday, November 4. It will then travel to New York, where it will open at Gagosian’s new Madison Avenue gallery on November 14, in conjunction with the fall auction season.
The exhibition features portraits of Michael Chow by Keith Haring and David Hockney, who are pictured here at Mr Chow’s Art Dinner in New York. Hockney’s “Portrait of Michael Chow” is a half-length portrait drawn from life by the artist, while Haring’s “Mr. Chow as Green Prawns in a Bowl of Noodles” was composed by Haring in his signature style of dynamic lines and vibrant colors to depict three versions of the restaurateur in a bowl of one of the house’s specialty dishes. Follow the link in our bio to learn more. __________ #KeithHaring #DavidHockney #Gagosian @keithharingfoundation (1,2) David Hockney, “Portrait of Michael Chow,” 1969 © 2026 Estate of David Hockney. Photo: Owen Conway; (3) David Hockney and Keith Haring at Mr Chow’s Art Dinner, New York, April 1985. Photo: © Ben Buchanan. All rights reserved 2026/Bridgeman Images; (5,6) Keith Haring, “Mr. Chow as Green Prawns in a Bowl of Noodles,” 1986 © Keith Haring Foundation. Photo: Josh White (@joshuawhitephotography)

item.title: @schomburgcenter: November is Puerto Rican Heritage Month. It’s a great time to learn about the activism of
item.author: @schomburgcenter
item.description:
November is Puerto Rican Heritage Month. It’s a great time to learn about the activism of our namesake Arturo Schomburg, a Puerto Rican–born Black scholar and bibliophile.
Did you know that Mr. Schomburg, along with friends Rafael Serra, Rosendo Rodríguez, and Silvestre Pivalo founded the political club Las Dos Antillas in 1892? They advocated for the liberation of Puerto Rico and Cuba from Spain. Mr. Schomburg served as the group’s secretary. Meeting minutes document donations of medical supplies, money, and weapons in aid of their independence.
A few pages of Mr. Schomburg’s notes are in our Digital Collections. Our Jean Blackwell Hutson Research and Reference Division has the group’s meeting minutes on microfilm. A research appointment is not needed to view. #PuertoRicanHeritageMonth #PRHM #ArturoSchomburg #Schomburg #PuertoRico

item.author: @hankwillisthomas

In a real sense all life is inter-related. All men are caught in an inescapable network of mutuality, tied in a single garment of destiny. Whatever affects one directly, affects all indirectly. I can never be what I ought to be until you are what you ought to be, and you can never be what you ought to be until I am what I ought to be... This is the inter-related structure of reality - #mlk
A moment from my walkthrough of LOVE OVER RULES. What binds us goes deeper than our divisions, and the ideas we put into the world, conscious or unconscious, are infectious.

item.author: @dancetheatreofharlem
item.description:
Our Sunday Matinee is coming up on November 8th and we are so excited to welcome the Limón Dance Company as one of our special guest performers!✨
Founded in 1946 by José Limón and Doris Humphrey, the Limón Dance Company has been at the vanguard of American Modern dance since its inception and is considered one of the world’s greatest dance companies. The Company will present two excerpts from Mazurkas, a work of exuberant and musical dancing in tribute to the people of Poland’s heroic spirit in their revival after World War II, performed by former DTH School student Stephen Haley, Olivia Mozie, and Joey Columbus.
We are so excited to have them join us for an afternoon of artistry, made for the whole family. Get your tickets for Sunday Matinee on our website today!💙
Photos by Kelly Puleio

item.title: @phillipsauction: In ‘True Blonde IV (At Home)’, Lisa Yuskavage presents a vision of femininity that is at o
item.author: @phillipsauction
item.description:
In ‘True Blonde IV (At Home)’, Lisa Yuskavage presents a vision of femininity that is at once hyper-feminine and curiously restrained. ​
The 1999 painting features her childhood friend and recurring subject Kathy, whose upward gaze and delicate gold cross lend her an introspective, devotional quality. Working in soft chiaroscuro, Yuskavage brings the visual languages of classical painting and popular imagery into dialogue, complicating the distinction between the idealized and the actual, the beautiful and the exaggerated.​

item.title: @alminerech: #SundayRepost #RichardPrince
item.author: @alminerech
item.description:
#SundayRepost #RichardPrince
•
On Sundays, we do reposts from our shows or artists represented by the gallery that you posted on IG. Tag us and we will select the best shots and share them on our feed!
•
Here are photos shared by @experimentacultura, @_fewcolors and @dosgirlsontherun, featuring ‘Richard Prince: Tell Me Everything’ at Museo Jumex in Mexico City, Mexico, on view through February 7, 2027. The first major survey show of the artist in Latin America, ‘Richard Prince: Tell Me Everything’ is arranged around in-depth explorations of the artist’s most iconic series—“Cowboys,” “Girlfriends,” “Jokes” and “Cartoons”—that have been present over more than 40 years of Prince’s career.
Prince has been working as an artist since the 1970s; a member of the influential Pictures Generation, he worked alongside other artists to expand the scope of conceptual photography through the use of appropriation and rephotography. Prince takes aim at the vulgar, revealing culture’s indiscretions—misogyny, consumerism, exhibitionism and idealized desire. However, as a critique it is ambiguous in that it is accompanied by an equal dose of sympathy and obsession. He is an avid collector and curator of Americana. In selecting or regroupings images, whether they be rephotographs of advertisements or forged publicity photographs, extracting them from their source, Prince elevates them to the status of fine art. As Robert Rubin writes “He appropriates an era and makes something that resonates differently for different people. The beauty of Richard Prince’s art is that it doesn’t have limits.”
•
Thank you for sharing!
•
#Repost #AlmineRech

item.title: @gagosian: Two significant presentations of work by Irving Penn are currently on view in Paris at Bou
item.author: @gagosian
item.description:
Two significant presentations of work by Irving Penn are currently on view in Paris at Bourse de Commerce (@boursedecommerce) and Maison Européenne de la Photographie (@mep.paris).
At Bourse de Commerce, “Le monde selon Penn” features almost 450 of Penn’s photographs from the Pinault Collection, tracing his production from the 1940s to the early 2000s. The presentation is part of “Remember Me,” a major group exhibition organized in celebration of the bicentenary of photography.
At Maison Européenne de la Photographie, “Penn & Fashion” features Penn’s photographs of Parisian haute couture collections, as well as his collaboration with the Japanese designer Issey Miyake (@isseymiyakeofficial), whose sculptural garments perfectly complemented Penn’s minimalist photographic style. Follow the link in our bio to learn more about these exhibitions. __________ #IrvingPenn #Gagosian @the.irving.penn.foundation (1-4) Installation views, “Le monde selon Penn,” Bourse de Commerce, Paris, October 7, 2026–January 10, 2027.
